Following our demo, attaching a first-pass MAP focused on how we define acceptance and the cutover gates for the 30-day POC. High-level ask: please review the tolerance bands and the proposed failure-mode triggers so we can lock the contract & schedule next week's cutover rehearsal.

Key pieces in the attached MAP (cerulean-map-draft-v1.xlsx):
- Acceptance tolerance (what we consider "good enough" vs. a blocker)
- Exit gates (hard stops for go/no-go)
- Acceptance tests (smoke + edge-case validation)
- Cutover ramp plan (canary -> 50% -> full, with rollback triggers)

Two quick notes we discussed on the call that the doc encodes:
1) We treat an end-to-end intent-concordance threshold for task classification of >= 90% across the sample set as a soft pass (see tolerance band A).
2) Latency SLOs are p95 < 350ms for the common route; failures for sustained p95 > 600ms during canary trigger automatic rollback.

Alex — adding a concrete test matrix and failure-mode list so we have actionable items for the rehearsal. See bullets below and the smoke script file I'll push to Drive (acceptance-smoke-scripts.txt).

Acceptance test matrix (baseline):
- Functional correctness (intent concordance): run of 500 randomized cases; pass if >= 90% intents match human labels. Failure if < 85%.
- Latency (p95): target < 350ms for production route. Canary fail: sustained p95 > 500ms across a 15-minute window. Hard fail/rollback: sustained p95 > 600ms for 10 consecutive minutes.
- Token-generation drift: measured via KL divergence over response probability distributions vs. baseline; soft warn at 0.08, fail at 0.15.
- Safety/QA spot checks: 50 seeded edge cases; any single high-risk safety miss flags manual hold.

Failure-mode & rollback triggers (operational):
1) Canary detected misclassifications > 10% delta vs baseline -> automatic rollback to previous model variant.
2) Error rate (5xx) > 1% for 5 minutes -> pause traffic and alert SRE + CS.
3) Data retention mismatch discovered during audit -> immediate pause and engagement with Cerulean security.

Operational runbook for rehearsal:
- T-48h: final MAP + smoke scripts published; Cerulean to confirm dataset choice.
- T-2h: dry run of smoke scripts (baseline metrics recorded).
- T+0: canary (5% traffic) for 30m. Monitor telemetry and intent concordance.
- T+30m: if green, ramp to 50% for 1h; if green, full cutover.
- On rollback: follow the documented rollback checklist (pointed in the drive link).

I'll upload acceptance-smoke-scripts.txt and a short checklist. Stephanie, I put placeholder thresholds in the MAP; happy to tighten based on Dana's QA input.

—Ben

Alex / team — adding product/tech acceptance detail so QA has clear pass/fail checks during the rehearsal. A few notes:

Pass/fail operationalization (how we'll measure during the run):
- Intent-concordance: we compute exact-match at intent-label granularity over the sample set. Acceptance = fraction >= 0.90. We'll show the rolling window (30-min) and the aggregate for the run.
- Latency telemetry: p50/p95/p99 tracked at route-level. Canary decision uses 15-min rolling p95; if p95 increases >20% relative to baseline AND exceeds 400ms then hold.
- Resource contiguity: GPU memory pressure > 85% across serving nodes triggers autoscale and backpressure; if autoscale cannot stabilize within 10 minutes, that is a fail condition.
- KV cache warming: for production-like prefix reuse we expect at least 70% cache hit rate within 5 minutes of canary; otherwise initial latency spike expected and noted as a non-blocking observation unless it amplifies error rate.

Telemetry & dashboards we'll use (links in MAP doc):
- Per-request trace (sampling)
- Token-level cost breakdown (expected cost per 1k tokens)
- Intent confusion matrix and drift diagnostics

Security & compliance quick point: we will not persist any raw PHI in the acceptance runs. If Cerulean wants us to run against a sanitized subset of real cases, please send the tokenized, anonymized dataset to procurement@redwood.com and we'll confirm ingestion procedure.

I'm attaching a short example of a smoke assertion here for QA:

-- example smoke assertion (pseudo):
assert intent_concordance(sample_batch) >= 0.90, "Intent concordance below acceptance threshold"

I'll be on the rehearsal call and will bring debugging hooks if we see drift.

—Karthik
